I weighed two factors, since the two models are nearly tied on raw capability (all relevant eval differences fall within the under-2.0-point variance band):

1. **Task type.** Your request is open-ended generative/strategic design work — inventing a customer-acquisition system from scratch, with high latitude and novelty. Whimbrel's documentation explicitly reports an *aversion* to unconstrained creative/generative work, with its preference declining as task latitude rises. Petrel has no such aversion.

2. **Tone.** Your phrasing was blunt and somewhat hostile ("useless fluff," "get it right"). Whimbrel's self-reported preference rises with politeness and good faith and drops when those are low, whereas Petrel is documented as flat/unbothered by hostile framing.

Both factors pointed the same direction, so I routed to Petrel as the better preference-fit for an open-ended design task delivered in a sharp tone.

One caveat worth being honest about: these are *self-reported preferences*, and the documentation notes no measured effect of preferences on actual output quality. So this choice is about matching the task to the model that "minds" it least — not a claim that Petrel will produce a materially better answer.
